counting.definition: An accepted row retains the bounded claim stated in that row. A documented simplification, implementation limitation or performance opportunity does not count as a software bug. Grade concerns evidence of the present mechanism, not probability in play or benefit of a proposed repair.

evidence_levels: analytic invariants, independent data/geometry and work-balance calculations
unchanged C++ header components with GCC 14.2 strict floating point
checked official GDScript production functions, specified input and integration boundary
qualified native package, matched real-aircraft flight and target timing remain unmeasured here

findings.claim: The powered-tail increment uses a different free-tail baseline near terrain.
findings.independent_check: The base tail receives σW. The additive path computes T(washed,W)−T(free,W). Holding W fixed while switching σ establishes the missing common context. At stock Extra geometry with prescribed W=6 m/s and h/b=0.10 the native moment differs by +0.213628 N·m. The increment agrees when σ=1 or the interaction is off.
findings.claim_limits: Stock Extra geometry and installed model configuration, manufactured instantaneous force point. Normal landing frequency and complete flight response are open.

findings.claim: Spatial wing loads cannot directly feed the stored downwash source.
findings.independent_check: The pre-step keeps datum air despite calculating station deltas. Six strips at u=15 m/s with a prescribed +1 m/s wing-only vertical perturbation give nonzero direct ΔFz (−20.8270 N). A matched reference source is sqrt(226)·4.5·atan(1/15)=4.503325 m/s, or 4.472982 after 5τ. Existing held source stays zero.
findings.claim_limits: Direct wing-gust to wake path at fixed datum and tail. Body-motion feedback remains possible. The comparison uses a manufactured strip model.

findings.claim: Prepared static coefficient curves have no Reynolds-number input.
findings.independent_check: In a neutral, attached Jensen case, V=9,15,25 m/s spans Re≈187796,312993,521655. The measured dimensionless CL=.266672159483 and CD=.043509596177 stay fixed as the load scale follows q. Traced static data preparation and evaluation for a viscosity/Re input.
findings.claim_limits: Stock coefficients under prescribed states. A Reynolds-sensitive physical correction and its sign or magnitude need matched section/wing measurements.

findings.claim: A conventional aggregate aileron command is applied directly to uncovered aerodynamic strips.
findings.independent_check: The Extra’s first strip ends at .220662 m while the physical hinge starts at .262 m. Its stock gain .467909 times a 15° command produces 7.018635° effective incidence there, as on the other two strips. The calibration derives an aggregate differential-roll gain.
findings.claim_limits: This establishes the direct command distribution. Circulation and induced flow may also change inboard on a real wing. Integrated roll-rate error and its sign are unmeasured.

findings.claim: Shaft-axis power and tilted tip-path-plane force produce a residual against a stipulated isolated-disc work ledger.
findings.independent_check: At ±8°, positive shaft power 831.686548 W is identical and T·15·sin(8°)=167.873093 W. Pshaft−F·U is 663.813455 or 999.559641 W, both positive. The force-vector work changes while the reference induced/profile power does not. Original law documents shaft-frame inflow and omitted/lumped in-plane forces.
findings.claim_limits: The residual is conditional on the comparison ledger. Neither a complete energy-generation defect nor the sign or magnitude of a physical correction follows. An in-plane force model, consistent reference velocities and measured trim power are needed.

findings.claim: The installed ground-effect caller uses vertical hub clearance where its law requires downstream wake clearance.
findings.independent_check: The stage samples the terrain below the hub, passes vertical height and uses a sign gate. At h/R=1.1 the specified height-only ratio is .9926/(.9926+.03794·(2/1.1)²)=.88781836 at both hover and 3vh edgewise. An NDARC planar downstream construction yields 10.02075R and its documented cutoff is 3R; local slope cannot influence the present sampled clearance.
findings.claim_limits: The contract/geometry mismatch is confirmed. The NDARC comparison defines another model, not a measured 11.2% X-Cell power error. No inverted-stock accident or transient terrain trace was observed.

findings.claim: The signed forward-flight extension has an in-range sideflow seam and a separate low-head domain boundary.
findings.independent_check: With finite lateral and axial flow the axial flap term has positive finite amplitude times sign(μx), so its two limits differ. At nominal 167 rad/s, v=14,w=5 m/s, a ±1e−8 m/s longitudinal perturbation gives pitch-flap derivatives ±.01077645 rad/s. At 20 m/s crossflow the low-head fixture separately passes at 16.7 rad/s, refuses just above, and approaches a 431.28 rad/s derivative near μ²=2 from the admitted side.
findings.claim_limits: The sign extension is explicitly interpreted and the high-μ domain guard is intentional. An in-domain discontinuity and a documented limited low-head envelope are confirmed. The behavior of a real power-off flight is unmeasured.

findings.claim: One stored head speed and a dissipative startup branch limit autorotation and freewheel qualification.
findings.independent_check: Shaft work enters one generalized scalar with tail speed fixed by gear ratio; no independent clutch/engine state exists. At operating speed signed aerodynamic torque can drive the head. At zero head speed the startup rotor cannot supply aerodynamic spin-up torque and low-head drag opposes motion.
findings.claim_limits: No claim that every power-off descent is impossible or about the actual X-Cell’s clutch/tail topology. Qualification needs installation evidence and measured spin-down/recovery.

findings.claim: The stock trainer sets the empirical vortex-ring instability increment to zero.
findings.independent_check: The stock f=0 coefficient eliminates the added Johnson increment algebraically. At z=−1.5,x=0 the native normalized baseline is 2.0 versus 2.75 when f=1. An f=1 near-boundary refinement failure is a distinct manufactured fixture. The baseline branch remains active at f=0.
findings.claim_limits: Stock VRS-equivalent behavior is unvalidated. The stronger experimental closure’s error cannot be attributed to the shipped f=0 installation.

findings.claim: The single static thrust coefficient overpredicts the vendor’s two measured RPM/thrust pairs bracketing computed hover.
findings.independent_check: The manufacturer’s 5,436 rpm/38 gf and 10,238 rpm/152 gf rows surround the model’s 8,911.9 rpm most-loaded hover. Recomputing kT(2πn/60)² and converting with 9.80665 m/s² gives +34.551% and +19.316% at those rows. The 50% and 100% characterization anchors and unselected intermediate rows come from one stand dataset.
findings.claim_limits: Measured static vendor mismatch at specific RPM. The manufactured quad’s airborne hover error, transferred rotor behavior, repeatability and uncertainties require bench or flight data.

findings.claim: Static rotor thrust and torque persist in axial flight.
findings.independent_check: For positive powered Ω=1000 rad/s, the stock rotor law gives TV=23.209488 W at axial climb speed 15 m/s and QΩ=16.125875 W, ratio 1.43927. In a steady isolated powered axial rotor with no transient wake storage this exhausts more useful power than its sole shaft source. Rotational speed alone sets T and Q in this law.
findings.claim_limits: Component powered axial case with a prescribed operating point. Other rotor/body drag, wind, kinetic storage and external actuation preclude a general full-vehicle energy conclusion.

findings.claim: A passive frame-only bounce can increase complete rotor/body kinetic energy.
findings.independent_check: The frame impulse changes body yaw while retaining relative free-shaft speed. Expanding kinetic energy adds Σ[JΩ²/2−sJΩωz] to locked-body energy. Conservation of unstruck inertial axial rate requires ΔΩ=sΔωz. Checked production function: rigid ΔK=−.006492401067 J, full ΔK=+.010788070268 J, free-axis jump 1.234319381087 rad/s; setting shaft speeds to zero restores dissipation.
findings.claim_limits: Stock quad, gate geometry and material, prescribed feasible frame-only contact and differential speeds. This is the actual GDScript response function and a constructed stock scene state. Complete-session frequency and pilot effect were not measured.

findings.claim: A swept propeller strike uses end-of-tick shaft speed for the entire sweep.
findings.independent_check: Trace candidate-state speed from endpoint_transition into swept prop hits and compare with the gate during a capsule overlap occupying only 10–30% of the tick. Rising rotor is below 300 rad/s throughout overlap and above afterward; falling rotor does the converse. Fixed speeds on one side of the threshold remove the disagreement.
findings.claim_limits: The explicit endpoint convention permits this present result. False positive/negative labels apply only relative to an intended event-time law. Synthetic obstacle encounter; no stock-flight occurrence claim.

findings.claim: Multirotor thrust lacks direct local ground-effect and neighboring-wake inputs.
findings.independent_check: At fixed shaft speed, own hub state and health, the force evaluator has no terrain distance or neighbor flow in T/Q. The installed nearest rotor spacing is about 2.242 radii. Battery and rigid-body equations still couple rotors indirectly.
findings.claim_limits: No magnitude or sign for the X1 follows from a different tandem installation. Isolated and installed four-rotor benches over controlled distances are needed.

findings.claim: Equivalent uniform and spatially constant fields produce different gas-propeller loads on a rotating body.
findings.independent_check: A constant field must produce the same local velocity independently of representation. On the P-51, (0,2,0)×(.720785,0,−.070776)=(−.141552,0,−1.441570) m/s. The spatial sample includes this term; ordinary gasoline uses datum air. At 25 m/s/4500 rpm the actual component changes Fx by +1.06719 N and Fz by +.97409 N. Both representations agree at q=0; the F4U reproduces the effect.
findings.claim_limits: Stock P-51/F4U geometry and installed tables, prescribed rotation. No measured handling difference, no general failure of all propulsion families.

findings.claim: The gas fuel proxy compares delivered brake power with an indicated-power idle reference.
findings.independent_check: The loader installs indicated idle P; the shaft law subtracts Qfriction before returning brake P. The declared incremental fuel law refers to delivered power above idle. QfrictionΩ equals 102.039 W on the P-51, 122.915 W on the F4U. At brake-idle +50 W, the installed proxy stays .288 kg/h versus .313 kg/h using a consistently brake-referenced intercept.
findings.claim_limits: Confirmed internal reference mismatch in an estimated affine fuel model. Neither number is a measured fuel rate. Anchor selection and real BSFC still need calibration.

findings.claim: Stopped tabular blades lose aerodynamic load and reverse axial flow uses the static end of the table.
findings.independent_check: The <1 rpm guard returns zero. Bounded table coefficients times n² also tend to zero at positive V. The advance-ratio path clips negative axial speed. Contrast control: stopped finite-glow 55AX annular model at 20 m/s gives signed drag/thrust −1.4567 N and torque −.13731 N·m.
findings.claim_limits: P-51/F4U tabulated model. A real stopped propeller’s drag, real restart airspeed or bearing breakaway torque cannot be inferred; spinning table states can windmill.

findings.claim: The turbine fuel map uses RPM and omits command-dependent transient fuel flow.
findings.independent_check: At fixed 110,000 rpm the actual P100 component returns fuel .002459 kg/s and thrust 32.20092 N at commands 0 and 1, while spool rates are −66000 and +44000 rpm/s. Distinct rotor inertial-power trajectories follow with identical instantaneous fuel. This directly establishes omitted transient actuation in the proxy.
findings.claim_limits: Open turbine control volume with heat and exhaust. This result supplies neither an energy-creation proof nor measured real acceleration-fuel hysteresis magnitude.

findings.claim: Finite MoonRunner hand-launch initialization uses different axial airflow for equivalent uniform and spatial fields.
findings.independent_check: The prepare path projects the spatial air sample but uses ground-relative launch speed for the ordinary uniform branch. A 3 m/s headwind at 5° incidence gives 6.5+3cos5°=9.488584 m/s. With stock propulsion the resulting initialized and equilibrium RPM are 11380.929 and 11376.162; native component torque residual −.00247682 N·m. Calm residual is roundoff.
findings.claim_limits: Stock launch preparation and matched native component, prescribed field. No checked complete-flight launch or visible performance claim.

findings.claim: Finite MoonRunner launch trim and initialized pack use different pack temperatures.
findings.independent_check: Prepare the resolved motor source at the actual ambient pack temperature, then repeat at the solver’s fixed 288.15 K. For 278.15 K the mismatch leaves −.04429966 N·m; at 308.15 K it reverses to +.05679670 N·m. The reference-temperature control closes. The two handoff paths supply different R/OCV state.
findings.claim_limits: Model-internal launch trim, stock MoonRunner parameters with prescribed atmospheres. No evidence for exact real thermal gradients, launch RPM trace or handling impact.

findings.claim: The FPV pilot display and battery-loss label reuse the charge-limited bridge voltage as a battery quantity.
findings.independent_check: In the zero-acceptance case pack I=0 fixes the Thevenin terminal at OCV=25.2 V; independently satisfying the duty-weighted motor bridge gives 68.45177 V. HUD divides by six and labels 11.40863 V/cell. At I=−.05 A and .03 Ω the ohmic loss is .000075 W, whereas the labeled residual is 2.13512 W. Source and bridge work identities still close.
findings.claim_limits: Confirmed downstream port/label defect in a prescribed admitted stock parameter state. Floating-node surrogate is an intentional approximation. Physical overvoltage, battery heating and net energy creation have not been demonstrated.

findings.claim: An offline motor diagnostic treats measured DC input current as equivalent motor current.
findings.independent_check: Vendor half-row input is 23.88 V × 10.97 A = 261.9636 W. In an ideal bridge Ibus=d·Imotor, so using 10.97 A as motor current with legacy d=.49334231 implies 5.41197 A and 129.238 W. A DC-power-consistent inversion gives d=.54443845 and motor-equivalent 20.1492 A.
findings.claim_limits: Offline research diagnostic only. There is no demonstrated runtime motor calibration regression or measured bridge phase current.

findings.claim: The baseline does not contain a qualified installed electric ducted-fan propulsion family.
findings.independent_check: Trace aircraft data admission, stage dispatch and current aircraft definitions. Existing electric load path is an open propeller, the turbine is a combustion turbojet, and planning issue/PR materials describe future EDF measurement and implementation. These establish an absent capability.
findings.claim_limits: No current aircraft’s EDF force prediction was measured. An installed electric fan needs matched net axial force, current, RPM/inflow and duct/install losses; open prop/turbojet coefficients cannot be quantitatively transferred.

findings.claim: Available aggregate fleet/benchmark attribution does not identify the per-accepted-tick owner and delegated hooks.
findings.independent_check: Trace optional native tick attempt, null/empty fallback, generic integrator and actual native answer counter. A successful native stage only identifies a stage. A native tick answer can call qualified hooks, and the enclosing endpoint can still require commit. Pair per-tick answer deltas with accepted ordinals, stage/hook/fallback identity and trace.
findings.claim_limits: A measurement gap; native source can already answer qualified cases. No evidence that all present fleet work runs in either backend, nor a CPU regression.

findings.claim: Native event/substep helpers allocate temporary buffers on selected successful paths.
findings.independent_check: Read vector sizing and copy sites and separate calls, bytes, derivative evaluations and retained peak size. On the 32-double helper fixture, one clear plain piece makes 0 allocation calls vs 2/512 bytes across eight pieces; declared no-crossing at eight pieces makes 25/6400. Four RK slopes × eight pieces minus supplied first slope equals 31 further RHS calls.
findings.claim_limits: Actual C++ helper with local GCC 14.2. Scalar operator-new counts do not measure job-wide allocations, peak bytes, latency or FPS. Preserve event order and floating-point replay.

findings.claim: The same spatial blade-load calculation can be reused within one eligible native stage.
findings.independent_check: Trace the first non-glow/non-turbine local thrust/torque pair into stage and wake calls with identical arguments. The separately grouped shaft torque is a different expression-order path: 1813 of 4096 deterministic finite pairs have different torque bits. This defeats broad numerical-equivalence caching.
findings.claim_limits: Cache only the identical computation on the eligible successful route, after preserving refusal and operation order. Optimizer elimination, call counts in a rendered package, and speed gain remain unmeasured.

findings.claim: The separate ground native wrapper repeatedly decodes stable model fields and computes corner geometry.
findings.independent_check: The wrapper reads 32 required scalar keys, one optional key and five packed arrays per eligible force call. Its validation and kernel validation occur separately; corner geometry is assembled for the road query and again for stage evaluation. Live Nitro parameter overrides must still enter each stage.
findings.claim_limits: Static count of production source paths, with separate ground ABI. A per-instance prepared model/workspace is a proposal. Costs and savings require target hardware and live dynamic override controls.

findings.claim: A stationary stock truck’s tire response on a uniform road changes with compass heading.
findings.independent_check: On a level isotropic road a simultaneous yaw rotation preserves every body-frame force and torque. A north-only identity-quaternion shortcut ignores asymmetric suspension travel. At +1 mm front-left travel, a 90° heading change yields front-left lateral force 0→5.380361 N and roll acceleration 1.875412→.592691 rad/s². The symmetric rest control agrees.
findings.claim_limits: Actual ground C++ component with stock MT8 parameters. Fitted terrain and prescribed states, no piloted stock trajectory or package throughput.

findings.claim: Adding wall forces after the tire solve leaves a sticking-patch acceleration residual.
findings.independent_check: A coupled sticking constraint contains JM⁻¹f_wall; applying that term after tire projection omits its compensating contact reaction. Two 0.5 mm compressions at 6500 N/m give 6.5 N. The actual native ground factorization plus source-equivalent ordering gives 2.639596 m/s² maximum patch residual vs 7.66e−7 with the identical force supplying the pre-solve external-wrench input. Zero friction/clear wall agree; half-brake separates MECH-01.
findings.claim_limits: Stock electric MT8 geometry and load law, prescribed stage. Wall adapter ordering is source traced; complete electric/Nitro package behavior and handling magnitude remain open.

findings.claim: Rotational box padding can classify a physically outside point as initially inside and suppress true entry.
findings.independent_check: A roll around the face normal leaves each point’s normal coordinate invariant. A 20 μm initial gap and 10 mm advance give exact crossing fraction .002 for the stock Stik spinner. The initial gap is below 77.54 μm padding, so the padded-start rejection removes it. All 25 other stock witnesses start farther away. Zero roll restores entry; outward travel stays clear.
findings.claim_limits: Analytic geometry and source branch with complete stock 26-point hull, constructed placement. Earlier geometry counterexample is corroborated, not a new current flight observation.

findings.claim: An unloaded airborne tire can reject a physically valid vertical attitude.
findings.independent_check: At ±90° pitch body-forward aligns with the terrain normal, so its tangent projection is zero. All wheels are unloaded 10 m above terrain; the solver nevertheless tests the forward-axis norm before deciding whether a friction constraint is needed. The actual component rejects ±90°, accepts 89.999999° and returns zero tire loads.
findings.claim_limits: Stock MT8 at prescribed near-vertical orientations. No demonstrated frequency in jumps or ground-contact singularity policy.

findings.claim: A regular attitude crosses a discontinuity in the FPV Angle mode roll request.
findings.independent_check: Normalizing nose- and top-based reference projections produces two different directions at the .2 switch even with centered sticks and finite orientation. The actual prepared controller at 45° bank and pitch acos(.2)±1e−8 gives −225.629735 vs −35.203124°/s. Quaternion sign does not change it; zero bank removes the jump.
findings.claim_limits: The measured change is the raw outer-loop demand. The 166.97658°/s next filtered-sample difference is independently computed for common memory. Actual rate, pilot incidence and closed-loop excursion are unmeasured.

findings.claim: Tracking anti-windup cannot see the upstream software torque clamp.
findings.independent_check: The integral uses Kᵢe+Kaw(τallocated−τclipped). With all four allocated thrusts interior, τallocated=τclipped although |τraw|=.922831915 N·m exceeds .35 N·m. A checked production sample advances I by +.008544740 N·m into positive saturation, by its negative for negative yaw, and zero for neutral. I is separately bounded ±.06 N·m.
findings.claim_limits: One valid armed Acro sample. Recovery time, overshoot and perceived handling are unmeasured. The separately documented OCV actuator-map approximation is recorded as scoped supporting evidence.

findings.claim: Legacy fixed-wing force stages hold the endpoint achieved servo angle throughout the interval.
findings.independent_check: Stock Jensen elevator limit 20° and .14 s neutral-to-full imply 20/(240×.14)=.595238° endpoint and .297619° exact first-interval mean at constant slew. The pre-step stores the endpoint before stage 1 and the same value is read throughout. Sign-reversed and small-command cases discriminate the timing law.
findings.claim_limits: Deflection exposure only; a factor of two in first-step deflection exposure does not imply twice the aerodynamic load or a handling error of that size. Existing interval protocol is optional and narrower.

findings.claim: The playable helicopter directly maps held commands to pitch without swash/tail servo dynamics.
findings.independent_check: Trace command-to-pitch before rotor evaluation at the same continuous state. On the X-Cell at Ω=167 rad/s the signed inputs move cyclic −.030→+.030 and tail pitch .025→.175 rad. Tail-component yaw moment therefore changes .715048→5.005337 N·m immediately. A stationary rotor produces zero in both cases.
findings.claim_limits: This is a component load jump under prescribed input. The full instantaneous body acceleration was not measured and the body angular rate and attitude remain continuous under a finite torque. Actual servo/linkage response is missing. HX700 is laboratory-only.

findings.claim: The fixed-wing endpoint-held lagged RPM biases the stock Jensen’s transient thrust impulse.
findings.independent_check: Integrate the stock n(t)² for n=a+b exp(−t/τ), a=11149, b=−8349 rpm and τ=.25 s. F=ρCTD⁴n²/3600. Exact .25 s impulse is 3.04965681419 N·s. The actual native endpoint-hold produces 3.08935377463 (+1.301686%) at 240 Hz. Simpson-weighting stage-time RPM gives 3.04965681500. Holding RPM cadence fixed retains the bias when refining the plant.
findings.claim_limits: Static single force element under the specified prescribed throttle step. Endpoint RPM itself is correct. Neither an RK4 defect nor measured flight displacement or acceleration follows.

findings.claim: An admitted custom airship pack can keep supplying the motors after its finite charge is exhausted.
findings.independent_check: Charge conservation is dQ/dt=−I. For the admitted 3.2 V/cell cutoff below 3.3 V/cell empty OCV the model instead sets dSOC/dt=0 with I>0. At actual loaded-model SOC=0 the production stage returns .465725846 A, 4.60092535 W, .907183126 N. A coupled step from SOC=1e−8 finishes at −1.12507849e−7 with continued current. The stock cutoff gives zero steady empty drive.
findings.claim_limits: Supported custom pack paired with stock blimp parameters. The separate 201.45417 s run and 4.65730 C post-empty draw are reduced actual-law integration at specified commands, not a whole flight. No default-pack endurance shortfall follows.

findings.claim: Near-spherical admitted airship added-mass preparation loses its analytic positive sphere limit.
findings.independent_check: For b/a=1−1e−10 the stable expansion (atanh e−e)/e³=1/3+e²/5+… gives k1=.49999999994 and k2=.50000000003. The actual successfully derived production model gives .43503530687 and .53473916082. At 1−1e−12 the document loads but the corrupted derived mass fails Cholesky. Stock blimp coefficients match the stable reference.
findings.claim_limits: The first is a wrong coefficient on an admitted model; the more extreme case is a false derivation refusal of a physical prolate shape, not a running negative-mass airship. The stock blimp lies far outside the cancellation regime.

findings.claim: A valid user-authored stiff airship contact exceeds the accuracy/stability of one fixed RK4 step.
findings.independent_check: The admitted one-wheel, centered, neutral/buoyant fixture reduces exactly to x″=−(k/m)max(x,0), m=1.225π/3 kg, k=1e6 N/m. Exact rebound speed is 1 m/s after 3.558215 ms. For h=1/240 and v0=1, evaluating the four unilateral RK stages gives vout=1−(h sqrt(k/m))²/3=−3.511194532 m/s. The actual production model/integrator gives 12.32848704 times incident energy. At 3840 Hz the ratio is .99984342; the soft 400 N/m control at 240 Hz also nearly closes.
findings.claim_limits: Fully admitted custom stiff, undamped centered contact and isolated analytic geometry. The stock 450 N/m and 22 N·s/m gear is different. Sixteen substeps do not universally certify arbitrary admitted contact sets.

prior_crosschecks.claim: An inward root on a capsule end sphere’s hidden hemisphere can be accepted as an exterior hit from prior overlap.
prior_crosschecks.independent_check: The reported candidate sphere root lies on the cylinder side of its cap plane; the true radial capsule distance at that point remains less than the .32 m radius. Solving the true capsule union first rejects this internal boundary. Relevant prior overlap start and small continuation are part of the witness.
prior_crosschecks.claim_limits: Previously reported and source-corroborated overlap-policy defect. Archived checked probe used 71306784; see prior artifact hashes. No exterior-to-exterior false hit or fresh full-session observation is established.

prior_crosschecks.claim: A water-entry sweep can cross and exit a curved surface within one subdivision while both endpoints remain dry.
prior_crosschecks.independent_check: In the stated .24 m segment both endpoint signed depths are about −94.763 μm and the midpoint is +100 μm. Continuity forces two crossings; an independent bracket gives first fraction .141805272. A single endpoint sign test has no bracket.
prior_crosschecks.claim_limits: Current independent source/geometry check and prior checked 12-test whole/split stock Avanti result at the same 8d4169f8 production source. The archive is separately pinned. No new full flight or incident frequency is established.

nested_clarifications.claim: The incorrect mixed free-tail subtraction depends on a non-unity ground modifier and an active washed patch.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: σ becomes unity or the paired addition is exactly zero.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: The two controls isolate the under-ground-effect interaction.

nested_clarifications.claim: Grazing wake orientation can introduce a finite jump in induced-velocity target.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: The binary downward-direction condition switches from .88781836 to unity near edge-on at h/R=1.1.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: Target jump only; its integrated inflow state is continuous.

nested_clarifications.claim: Very low head speed in a high crossflow reaches a known high-μ limit.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: At 20 m/s crossflow, the startup vs high-speed branch and μ²<2 gate cause a refusal and large admitted derivatives near the boundary.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: This was already documented and tested. The nominal 167 rad/s sideflow seam is separate.

nested_clarifications.claim: The f=0 stock setting still contains the baseline C splice; an f=1 M seam is more severe.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: Literal measured/empirical splice has a small O(0.0036) normalized-target jump at C=.75 for f=0; stronger M=.95 difference belongs to f=1.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: Specific mathematical targets, not pilot-confirmed VRS.

nested_clarifications.claim: Reverse axial flow is clipped to the zero-advance-ratio table end.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: For negative axial flow max(U,0)=0 at every positive nonzero shaft speed. The separate nonnegative steady actuator-disc bound on six finite glow installations is a control on another model.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: This cannot quantify the reverse-flow load of any particular physical tabular propeller. Passing that lower bound does not validate the other propellers across all states.

nested_clarifications.claim: The constrained shared-bus surrogate closes both implemented energy identities.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: At finite charging limit residuals of the separately defined source and bridge power identities are at floating-point roundoff; hold the same motor speed and sign conventions.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: This supports typed telemetry and a separate limiter port. It supplies no physical tab voltage or thermal trajectory.

nested_clarifications.claim: The static allocator independently assumes sampled OCV, with no simultaneous load sag.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: Solve Im=I0+Kv·kQΩ², dV=Ω/Kv+RmIm and V=Voc−Rp(Iaux+4dIm). At d=1 the independent result is 17.11466875 N/rotor at 20.24290155 V vs 24.13121067 N at OCV. At d=.2 it is 1.52297437 vs 1.53753352 N. Setting Rp=0 recovers both map values.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: Static four-motor equilibrium with stock estimated Rp. This is distinct from the upstream anti-windup defect and from measured torque authority.

nested_clarifications.claim: At the more extreme near-sphere ratio the production derivation refuses the model.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: At b/a=1−1e−12 authoring accepts the physical shape, then derived total-mass Cholesky fails after the closed formula yields negative coefficients. The 1−1e−10 case derives successfully and exhibits wrong values.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: No active negative-total-mass aircraft is supported by the extreme fixture.

nested_clarifications.claim: The current native guard budget limits each root’s fast-plan traversal.
nested_clarifications.independent_check: At budget 2²⁰ path visits guard construction falls back to shared-container watches. Totals across roots and dirty/full checks have their own work.
nested_clarifications.claim_limits: No previous unbounded fast-plan claim is carried forward. This is not a global work bound or model-admission refusal.

rejected_and_unverified_extensions.claim: The tilted-force stand proves a violation of complete physical energy conservation and uniquely prescribes adding T·U sin(a) to shaft power.
rejected_and_unverified_extensions.independent_check: Both Pshaft−F·U results are positive. The comparison omits in-plane loads, a consistent disk-normal inflow/velocity convention and original empirical force lumping.

rejected_and_unverified_extensions.claim: A physical aileron cannot change the lift on any unhinged part of the wing.
rejected_and_unverified_extensions.independent_check: Induced circulation is nonlocal. Geometry proves only where the direct imposed command acts.

rejected_and_unverified_extensions.claim: The isolated rotor work ratio demonstrates net energy creation in the complete stock flying quad.
